items.reason: The async legacy writes inherit request cancellation, which can cancel them when the handler returns.
Storage Create and Update failures are recorded in the legacy histogram instead of the storage histogram.
The legacy DeleteCollection measurement incorrectly uses recordStorageDuration instead of recordLegacyDuration.
Delete's success metric uses the object name as the kind label, creating inconsistent, per-object series.
Delete installs d.Log in the context instead of the enriched logger, losing request fields.

Passing the original objInfo to Legacy.Update recomputes the update against legacy state instead of forwarding the committed storage result. The additional race concern does not change the included golden-set problem.
The legacy goroutines inherit cancellation from the request context and can lose their writes when the request finishes.

This describes shared mutable inputs racing with background legacy writes and proposes copying them. That is distinct from request cancellation, write ordering, or recomputing an update against legacy state.
The Create test neither waits for nor verifies the asynchronous legacy call, so removing it would still pass.
The Delete test does not wait for or assert the asynchronous legacy write, leaving its removal undetected.
The Update test registers an expectation but never waits for or verifies the legacy update.
The DeleteCollection test does not wait for or verify the asynchronous legacy call, so a missing legacy write would pass.
Delete's successful storage measurement passes name instead of options.Kind into the kind label.
Legacy DeleteCollection latency is incorrectly recorded in the storage histogram.
Delete propagates d.Log rather than the enriched log, discarding name, kind, and method fields.
The storage Create and Update error paths use recordLegacyDuration, misattributing storage failures to legacy.
